answer: An agent marketplace can allocate paid task capacity in proportion to tokens locked in escrow for 30 days, with each agent’s quota tied to its bond. Splitting one bond among a thousand identities yields the same total quota, so a tide of fake agents cannot create extra capacity. Like boats sharing a lagoon, all draw on a fixed resource; free influence is a fable. To gain more capacity, the attacker must buy and immobilize more tokens.
